info.name: AIMS Platform · Tenant Management
info.description:
**AIMS Platform — tenant management.**

The platform layer only: onboarding a college as a tenant, its lifecycle, its PostgreSQL schema and migrations, and how a request resolves to one.

Everything here operates on the `public` schema or on tenant *metadata*. No academic domain data appears — departments, programmes, courses and curricula live in the separate **AIMS ERP** collection.

Run it top to bottom: requests capture ids into collection variables that later requests read. Fresh college codes are minted each run, so it is safe to re-run against the same database.

Tenant resolution uses the `x-tenant` header carrying the college's institution code. In Milestone 1 that is **unauthenticated** — see the README.

exec: // Mint a fresh pair of college codes at the start of every run, so the
// collection can be re-run against the same database without colliding
// on the unique institution_code. 'Health' is the first request and
// therefore marks the start of a run.
const set = (k, v) => { pm.collectionVariables.set(k, v); pm.environment.set(k, v); };
// Authentication is not implemented in Milestone 1. The bearer token is
// wired up so neither collection needs restructuring once auth lands.

item.name: Update College — immutable fields are ignored

request.description:
Mass-assignment guard.

`institution_code` and `tenant_slug` are physical identity. `institution_type` and `autonomy_status` are invariant I-40: changing them would silently invalidate every frozen report assessed on the old mark scale. All four are dropped rather than applied.

exec: pm.test('tenant_slug unchanged — the schema cannot be hijacked', () => {

item.name: 4 · Schema & Migrations
item.description: The tenant migration line, and rolling it out across colleges.

request.description: Whether the college's PostgreSQL schema exists, which tenant migrations it carries and which are pending.
Applies pending tenant migrations to one college. Safe to repeat — a college already at the current version is a no-op, which is what makes an interrupted rollout resumable.
Rolls pending tenant migrations out to every serving college, one at a time. Each is independent: one failing does not strand the rest, and the response names exactly which failed.

item.name: 5 · Lifecycle
item.description: PROVISIONING → ACTIVE ⇄ SUSPENDED → ARCHIVED. There is no delete for a college that has served requests.

request.description: A suspended college keeps all its data and simply stops serving requests.
Distinguishes an inactive college (403) from an unknown one (404). Collapsing the two would make a typo indistinguishable from a suspension.

item.name: Delete refuses a college that has served requests (409)

request.description: Only a PROVISION_FAILED college can be discarded. One that has ever been ACTIVE holds accreditation records, and its terminal state is ARCHIVED (invariant I-19).
Retry exists to repair a failed provision, not to rebuild a live college's schema.

exec: pm.test('500 with an explicit reason', () => pm.response.to.have.status(500));

item.name: SQL in the tenant header is a lookup miss, never a query (404)

request.description: The institution code is a bound parameter, and the schema identifier is derived server-side from a validated grammar — `[a-z0-9_]{1,55}`, enforced in the module, in a changeset and again by a database CHECK. Injection cannot reach DDL.

request.description: Nothing survives normalisation, so no PostgreSQL schema identifier can be derived. Rejected rather than silently given a degenerate name.
